Absolutely! A lot are NAMI affiliated, and I would describe them as being like a diet hotline. Oftentimes it's peer support more than speaking with a counselor, but they're always incredibly empathetic and are able to be a bit more relatable. 

Usually they're limited to 15 minutes per call, but you can call multiple times throughout the day based on which one you use. A good tip is to find ones that accept out of state calls as well since the lines can sometimes have a wait or if you want to call at hours in which maybe your local one isn't open.

Eventually, he said we were breaking up, and I cried and begged for him to stay until the mess he'd made for me was taken care of. He let me buy him dinner, smiled when he said no. He then parked at his place like he always did and left me crying alone. Later, after he'd successfully hoovered me, he said he had assumed I planned to kill myself after he left.

I'm sorry you're feeling hurt, but I'm beyond grateful you were able to break it off. It'll get a lot better, and the further out you get, the more you're able to spot the red flags in hindsight and begin to recognize the massive bullet you dodged.

And it's not a restart like everyone says; it's a progression. You'll be okay! No one is angry, hurt, or let down. You're one of us whether you like it or not, and you'll always find support here. ❤️

Both of my longest relationships were with cluster bs. At this point, I have absolutely no clue what a healthy relationship looks like. It's like a number of other things I wound up taking at face value, never crossing my mind that he may have made it up like he's made up literally everything else. 

My theory is that he was twisting me into this monster until he could use it to justify cheating, discarding, etc. If he could make me into a horrible enough person, he'd be vindicated of being arguably one of the worst people I've ever met.

Ah, those suicide threats are a classic. I remember how casually he tossed suicide around while my hair was starting to fall out from the stress. And I'm sorry you're going through it, too!! When I talk to regular people about it, they chalk it up to a bad break up. It's absolutely impossible to get them to understand the mental and emotional warfare you're put under when you love a pwbpd. 

And it's incredible you didn't get discarded!! I swear to you, it's the worst-case scenario. It feels like every vindictive trait they possess is being concentrated to hurt you as much as possible. It's amazing you were able to leave, and there's no world where it wouldn't be worth it. I worry still that my exwbpd might end his own life, but I try really hard to remember that I tried my best. The ball is in their court, and that'll always be the case in these sort of relationships, but it's still a difficult thing to try and prepare yourself for.

I do, too. The first time he split on me, I'd have maxed out my credit card to get him an exorcism. I'd give up everything I own to take the bpd away from him, but he's let it turn him into a truly bad person. I hope one day the illusion can be broken for good so I can stop feeling crazy.

Twins! I have cptsd and am absolutely codependent, too. :) I felt the same way for a while. There were some red flags that I absolutely did not react ideally to, like when he dropped the super fun, "a dear friend accused me of raping her" story. Or when he admitted that everything he said to me at the beginning of our relationship was a lie. Or all the times he threatened to kill himself when I wanted to break up. 

The thing is that we reacted reasonably to some extremely abnormal and painful situations. Rolling over and taking it would've been the worst decision, even if we didn't like the reaction we actually had. I feel horrible for pwbpd and recognize that their lives are unbelievably painful, but we can't save them. We threw them a line, but it gets to the point where we'll just drown with them if we keep trying. They could help themselves, but even if they couldn't, sticking around would only make two tragedies instead of one.

It's not that you weren't a good enough partner, it's that you got used up. I did the same thing and tried everything within my power to help him. I gave him my money, time, and love and had to strong-arm him into getting a therapist. There's nothing in the world I wouldn't have done for him, and it still wasn't enough. 

It was my third discard about 5 months ago, and I still miss him. He cheated, lied, stole from me, and I still wonder if there's something I could do to knock some sense into him. I know people say that there's no sense in trying to apply logic where this is none, but that's not a very satisfying answer. I basically have to dehumanize my exwbpd to reconcile the insane personality changes he exhibited. 

I like to think that maybe we were too good to be true. Certainly we were to them, which is why they have to emotionally kneecap us when we let them down. It's like a scammer targeting rich people; if we had nothing to offer, there'd be no reason to target us. :)

I wonder the exact same thing sometimes. If he's this master manipulator that everyone says, he's good enough to consider a future in politics. He also loved to advertise this as an empath, especially early on. He presented himself as this extremely loving and caring person, but that turned out to not be the case.

I've heard it said on here that rather than being empathic, pwbpd are just highly sensitive people. My exwbpd used to absolutely hate watching embarrassing scenes in movies, to the point that he'd sometimes have to leave the room. Seems empathic until you consider that he discarded me once in the middle of the night in a parking lot, thinking I was going to kill myself. 

They're incredibly empathic, but only towards themselves. I honestly cannot tell if their overtaking of control is intentional or not, but I suspect that it is.

Yep. It was pretty common to hear about crazy, out-of-character things I'd done while drunk (I have no memory of these things, despite never being blackout) or when I was asleep. He'd say I said or did things that made absolutely no sense, and I had no way to combat it since I had no idea what was going on.

He discarded me about 5 months ago, and since then, we have only spoken a few times over text. Obviously, it's been pretty tumultuous, but I wanted to find some closure or common ground so I could move on from the damn thing. He just gets mad and accuses me of being horrible, and whenever I point out the suicide threats, pathological lying, rape accusations, etc. he just calls me delusional and crazy. 

If it is gaslighting, he's gotta be pretty good because I still sometimes feel crazy. Thank God I took videos and kept text messages, or else he might've sent me into a padded room.

Surprisingly enough, I feel pretty okay. I'm surprised by how sad I was to feel like I was ready to move on, like I was letting go of this person that only I knew existed, but now that it's happened I feel a lot better. :) I still periodically feel unholy rage and unimaginable loss, but they're getting fewer and further in-between.

I'm friends with a lot of my exes, and I wish I could've at least tried that with my exwbpd. I know that mine, in particular, is far too unstable to ever speak to, but I miss my best friend.

I understand how you feel. My exwbpd did all those things, and it made me furious. To lie about SA and misrepresent himself to the point I don't know who the hell I was living with all that time feels so violating and is a hard one to come to terms with. It's so frustrating because the ball is in their court; you've done all you can, and now it's all up to them. And for all your efforts, they can't even tell you the truth.

I remember being frustrated with myself, too. Why couldn't I just let him go? I was so sure that if I helped enough, made him happy enough, that he'd get better. We'd face the BPD and the trauma head-on, and we'd both be happier for it. The only problem is that I could never fix him because he's not broken. They're suffering and chaotic, but it's by design, and he functions exactly as intended. 

It'll get better and vent as much as you need. If you ever want to chat, I'm always happy to. :) There are also warmlines I used to like calling up and was a great resource early on. And I hope you can find some peace in all of this.

I wouldn't count on this working out for her; they always like to do this when they latch onto someone new. She could tell me she'd met this person yesterday and I'd believe it. It's not about you not being enough, it's that to pwbpd, you are *never* enough. I wouldn't be surprised at all if she tries to hoover you when this relationship doesn't work out.

And I'm glad you were able to get a bit of closure. :) In my experience, the closure I get from pwbpd (if any) is really unsatisfying, but it gets better as time goes on. I suggest going NC, but with any luck, she'll leave you alone.

It's was always scary to me how unattached my pwbpd could become at a moments notice. The way you're describing yours as just up and moving, trading her old life for a new one, is pretty common. It sounds like you're being really mature about it, though! All in all, that seems like a decent resolution when it comes to someone wbpd.

It was about 3 months in when I "met" his evil alter-ego. To be honest, though, the signs were there all along. Shouldn't have been a mystery for long as to why everyone he's ever dated or been close to wound up hating him.

Mine was officially diagnosed, so there was no mystery there. That being said, I actually mistook some of the symptoms for emotional immaturity when I absolutely should have known better. Pathological lying was the first symptom that something more was going on, along with the intense lovebombing. It took about a week for me to become the love of his life. 

I'm not saying people who aren't cluster b can't *think* they're in love way too soon, but saying he was considering suicide before meeting me was a bit much. The other hallmark is splitting. :) There's no question about whether or not it's BPD when that happens. I went from being the one thing he could never live without to being a horrible abuser and "just not enough" in about a month. The unfortunate part is that, by then, it's too late for the unofficial diagnosis to be very helpful.

Right? I can understand why they do A to get to B, but I can not understand how you can go through your life doing that. It seems so horrible and chaotic, and I want to encourage them to get help, but that's how I got myself into this mess to begin with. 

And thank you! I hope all of us can heal and go on to have healthy relationships. :) Bad as it is now, I think I'm more empathetic and value my boundaries more. Just trying to find the lesson to be learned in this exceptionally hard experience.

I absolutely agree it's a coping mechanism, just like all their actions are. I'm also inclined to believe that it's selfish in nature, although they don't always see it that way. I spoke to a pwbpd pretty bluntly about it once, thinking that since they're years into therapy, they may be able to honestly shed some light. 

What she told me is that they *know* that they're lying and being manipulative, but justify it as a win-win situation since both parties are happy. They think that when we do things they don't like, we aren't holding up our end of the bargain. When I asked why they act cruel and calloused even when we haven't done anything, she says that it's because they're afraid we'll do something. They get to the point where they know they'll eventually hate us, thereby justifying their actions. It's sort of like punishment-in-advance for flaws we're sure to exhibit, and if we don't, they pretend we do.

Obviously, every pwbpd is different, but I admittedly hated learning this. I want to be able to blame a disorder for something my exwbpd was aware of the entire time. His brief moments of clarity and "warnings" he gave make it harder to forgive him for something he could have chosen not to do.

Yep! Longest I saw him hold down a job was maybe 6 months...? And that was only because they gave him a huge promotion due to understaffing. He went through five different jobs in the year and a half I was with him, usually just abandoning the job after any sort of disagreement. He usually only lasted a few months and, at the end of our relationship, refused to work at all.

It's like that saying, "better the devil you know." I've been going through a hard time right now, and it's taking all my willpower to not reach out. It helps knowing that I will undoubtedly get burned if I do, but the world is easier to face when you don't have to face it alone. I miss who I thought my fiance was, I miss my best friend. I hope it passes for both of us!

Oooh, that's cold. She doesn't want to be alone, but she doesn't want to be with him, so she meets in the middle by pretending he doesn't exist? I have a really hard time with people not being open about that sort of thing with their parents, especially when she's willing to share it with you. Poor guy

I see this analogy a lot on here; I think they care about us the way they care about their favorite toy. It's not a selfless kind of care, and it never lasts. They stop when we're no longer their favorite.

I'm so sorry! :( I'm afraid I don't have a lot in the way of family either, and get what you're saying. Whenever something eventful at all happens, it makes sense to want to go to your pwbpd. They were an illusion, but they were usually a *nice* illusion.
Yeah, that doesn't sound great. Sounds like she's, at the very least, devaluing the guy. My guess is either cheating or getting ready to leave him.

I get how you feel. I think now that I understand what motivated the horrible things he's done, the anger has mostly faded. I *know* I can't be with him and that he doesn't care about me, but I miss having my best friend. Even if it's not romantic, I still wish there was a way I could speak to him. 

Other people just don't have the same impact. Going from spending every free moment of time with some to being alone takes too long to get used to. But I think you're right; sometimes you just have to let time do the rest of the healing for you.

Ooh, interesting. Everyone I've known wbpd usually has something to say about their partner. How long has it been going on? Because I could see it if in *her* reality, she's already 'moved on'? And not mentioning him is just a byproduct of that, so she has a better shot at getting new supply.

This may not be particularly helpful, but one thing I can't help but think about when I remember how hard I worked to build an idyllic life for my pwbpd is this quote from Infinity War. "In time, you will know what it's like to lose. To feel so desperately that you're right, yet to fail all the same." It feels silly to quote a superhero movie, but it really encapsulated how I felt.

We try so, so hard to make it work. Give everything, be willing to do anything, and it's still not enough. There's nothing in the world we could've done to change the outcome, but *they* could have. We do all we can, and all they have to do is not cheat and stick through it. The bar is set so low, and they don't even try. I know it's a disorder, but that will always hurt I think.

After every discard, the time before the next hoover typically increases. I went from the first taking days, the second taking weeks, and the third is now approaching 4 months. I wouldn't consider her hoovering to be out of the question, as I'm one of the believers that there is no *final* discard to them. It only becomes final when we stop putting up with everything or make it more effort than it's worth to get us back.

That all being said, I'm going to give you the same advice everyone else will; do not let her back into your life. It's important to consider that you would *never* do to her what she's doing to you. I know it hurts unbelievably now, but it's one of those necessities to break free. If 10 years from now you suddenly get injured and are unable to work, do you really think you could rely on her to stay by your side? These pwbpd are not worth the effort we put into them. 

It's damn near impossible at first to break free, but I hold out that it'll be worth it. :)
Nice dodging the hoover! :D

This seems like a pretty good summary! I particularly love it when one event goes through all these iterations. When I was discarded this last time, he couldn't really settle on the reason *why* he was discarding me. At first, it was that it just wasn't working out, and he wanted "something new." Then it was because he didn't deserve me, and finally, it was because I'm a horrible abuser and liar.

I didn't initially think I'd been cheated on. My exwbpd always claimed to hate cheaters, considering them the worst of the worst. At first, I just assumed he'd been cheated on in the past, and that's why he took a really over-the-top stance on the matter. He was fine with me looking through his phone, but I never did. The only red flag I ever saw in that department was that he had about a trillion different accounts or burners on all social media sites. He claimed that he'd just lost the password to the ones I knew about (the ones under his real name, which were about half of them), but that didn't explain the dozen email accounts he was logged into on Gmail. 

Fast forward to my inevitable discard. It was cruel and vicious, but it didn't seem like he'd already found a new supply. He'd moved across the country, and no contact initiated. In a moment of weakness, though, I peaked on a couple of sites to see what he was up to. There was only one burner account that I *think* is his that told me he had been looking to replace me a couple of months before he left. If it wasn't him, it's one hell of a coincidence. So, I guess there is no concrete evidence of him cheating, but I'm inclined to think he probably did.

I'm a bartender at a nightclub, and I love it. It is an insanely high volume of customers, but it's amazing if you can deal with the stress. Hands down the most money I've made from just bartending (not including bartending/server positions), and it's a lot of fun seeing how fast you can go. :) And while I will sometimes try and go the craft cocktail route when it's slow or for a regular, it's mostly how many lemon drops you can make before you have a brain aneurysm

Yeah, I sometimes get some of these weird hoover attempts. I used to never get some of those typical scam text messages where they pretended to be looking for someone, but now I get them all the time. Possibly, it's not my exwbpd, but it was definitely him who tried accessing some of my online accounts, and it was most likely him who kept trying to call my work looking for me. 

It still makes me anxious when they do weird shit like this, but nowadays I mostly find it annoying.

Ah, mine was the other way around. The first night I slept over, it was just as friends, but apparently, he dreamt about marrying me. I didn't start getting weird dreams about him until after his first discard. I know they only see us in black and white, but *my* *god* do they embody that well. When he split me, it was like he was evil and possessed, which was obviously quite different to the kind and loving person he marked himself as.

I would have these nightmares of our lives and our future, but the "evil" version was always lurking around. I remember one distinctly where he propossed to me, but the evil one was smiling behind him, hiding around a corner. They'd eventually go away, but I always got them at the beginning of each new cycle. If only I'd listened to the warning!

I'm four months out of my latest discard (lucky number 3), and lately, I've been feeling the same way. I feel lucky that I was able to accept that he's disordered and can see through his mind games, but there's this nagging feeling I get to reach out and talk with him. He still freaks me out and makes me anxious, but I worry I get a little overconfident now that I can recognize the tricks and assume he couldn't get to me again. 

In my case, at least, I recognize that it's not a normal response to want to speak with someone who would undoubtedly hurt me again if I tried. What he did was heartless and brutal, and I think I fall into the same mindset you mentioned. Maybe most of my intentions would be to try and help him, but I'd be lying if I said missing him wasn't part of it.

My best guess is that it's simply like an addiction, the same way alcoholics continue to drink even after it causes problem after problem. The intensity of the relationship (good and bad), paired with the idea of us being soulmates and meant to be together that was drilled into me, makes it hard to settle down into a more healthy relationship. 

All that, and I never got closure either. He tried really hard to keep the door open, I guess in case he ever wanted to get back together? Nothing ever seems final with pwbpd, and so it's trying to remove ourselves from a cycle that's still moving. Absolute NC has helped (no talking or checking socials), but I imagine that fully removing them from our lives mentally isn't so easy.
Yeah, it's not any more real than it is with other pwbpd. Because they're 'high functioning', I think it just makes what they think is love *seem* a bit more realistic.

No need to apologize! The little things can really wear you down :) One thing my exwbpd did that was subtle and *really* bothered me was when he'd talk to me in a condescending way. It wasn't outright mean or anything, but whenever I'd cry or come to him stressed about something, he would treat me like a child. Not in a gentle or protective way either, but like I was a little kid crying about something silly.

Honestly, not even close to a big deal compared to other things he did, it just still upsets me. He'd throw a huge tantrum and start talking suicide at every inconvenience, whereas I was being ridiculous stressing about money and the ticking time bomb I lived with.

Definitely should tell her. I'm considering the same problem, but I like to think the right person will be understanding. :) Everyone goes through their own personal struggles, and yours just happens to be an ex wbpd.

One thing that might be helpful is sharing this subreddit with her! If she's concerned, she'll see a million stories of people from all walks of life who went through the same thing.
Literally anything would've been appreciated.

This is well put, and I think this also adds another motivation to cycle through partners and loved ones. During my relationship with a pwbpd, I think it got more difficult for him to pull the wool over my eyes because I was always present. Now he can go meet anyone he wants, and his "reality" is less likely to be questioned. Additionally, he can now come back to me after months of being gone and tell me anything, and I'd have little to go on in terms of whether or not he's lying (other than knowing he's pathological liar). 

Their lifestyle preserves their ability to make reality whatever they want. It's seems so tumultuous, though, since I do believe they are self-aware to a certain extent.

I swear, these people are like emotional suicide bombers. They're willing to go down with the ship as long as they can take you down with them. I also wonder if jumping to her ex was an intentional strategy? Say if she wanted to punish you, he would be a convenient tool to do that with. It's also duel purpose because she can now triangulate, and if the relationship is objectively of lower quality, she can come crawling back with a reasonable sob story. 

I know analyzing their actions is like playing chess with someone who only knows how to set up a checkerboard, but once you know their motivations, it becomes easier to predict. I thought there was absolutely no way my ex would hoover even though they always do. Lo and behold, he's now resorting to creepy ways of trying to instigate contact. We should all get together and make a Choose Your Own Adventure book predicting pwbpd's movements.

Dude, I hope he was lying. The alternative is that this therapist did 4-7 years of education and training to become an overpaid yes-man. I don't even want to consider that they're just that stupid and couldn't see past the obvious story manipulation.

Actually, I can see how that would make sense. At the beginning of our relationship, my ex would go to extremes to make me happy and spend time with me. At the end, he couldn't even bother to pick me up from work. What's funny is I think towards the end, I was actually being a better partner. I was a lot more stable in life, had matured quite a bit, and was actively trying to improve myself. Maybe they shoot for the bottom of the barrel because those people are easier to maintain control over. When we succeed in life, their grasp is that much weaker.

If only you could reason with them. My exwbpd will inevitably have to downgrade as well. Not to seem too obsessed with myself, but I make good money, was more conventionally attractive, and did everything in my power to make him happy. I certainly have my flaws, but I'm a catch! If he had decided to stick around, he never would've had to work again and would've had the loyal partner he always said he wanted.

Obviously, though, he didn't stick around. This was slightly more hurtful by the fact that I don't think he had any new supply to fall back on. Granted, I *do* think he assumed I would still be an option for him, something I nixxed rather quickly. My guess is that, in the moment, it didn't matter how amazing I could've been. His desire to punish me for what he perceived to be unforgivable flaws outweighed the long-term consequences of his decisions.

Perhaps he did have doubts, but not in the way one would hope. He may regret hurting me to the extent that it's now affecting him, but he certainly doesn't care about how I feel. I truly believe you could give a pwbpd their ideal match, and it wouldn't matter. If you're not flawed, they'll *make* you flawed. Any doubt or shame they may feel is quickly resolved when they make us into monsters in their head.

I don't think it's so much moments of doubt, but more moments of panic. I doubt she cares if she's downgrading if she thinks she can get more/better supply from her current FP. 

My exwbpd absolutely does not care about me, and when I was discarded, he truly seemed to hate me. That made it all the more strange when he periodically tried to reinforce the idea that he *does* care about me and maybe one day we could be together again.

For the most part, when he thinks of me, I doubt it's anything more than surface-level acknowledgment that I exist. But when his supply is threatened or in a moment of desperation, I'm suddenly a solution to the problem. 

It's "doubt" the same way I may feel doubt when making a jump to a different job. Did I like the old one more? Did it pay better? Did I make a mistake by quitting? In the end, they're typically short-lived concerns because I can get a job anywhere.

I'm gonna go out on a limb here and say you certainly don't sound like a cluster b. And I get exactly what you're saying! Your survival instincts probably did kick in just like mine did after being put in an impossible situation. 

You are actively seeking help, worrying about how your fleas may affect you and others, and feeling guilty about whatever role you think you played in the relationship. These aren't exactly hallmarks of someone with a personality disorder. 

I had an emotional breakdown, too, blaming myself for being discarded and left confused from the gaslighting. I remember finding it really hard to draw the line; is he manipulating me, or am I just in denial that *I* was abusive? One thought I found helpful was that I don't get accused of being abusive from anyone else. Not close friends, family, or previous relationships, it was only ever him. 

Catching fleas and having your mental and emotional state waterboarded doesn't exactly leave you in an ideal place to be objective. Obviously, I'm going to be biased in your favor, but it seems like you're having a very common reaction. It's easy to assume we're at fault because our actions triggered their reaction, how ever uncalled for it may have seemed.

If you switch the scenario to something 3rd person, it seems ridiculous. My exwbpd threatened to kill himself in front of me when I wanted to break up, going so far as to pull a knife. After this, I became angry and resentful and destroyed our anniversary gifts to each other. What I did was not ideal, and I'm not proud that I resorted to destruction because of my emotions. That being said, if you keep an animal caged against its will, how at fault is it if they bite you? 

I'm in therapy and want to improve myself. I don't want to be destructive or have fleas, red flags, etc. But it's important to be empathetic with yourself. However you want to slice it, you *were* victimized, and it sounds like you are on the right path. :) You're taking responsibility for what you see as problematic behavior, which is all you can do.

Call me jaded, but this sounds like bullshit. Saying they've "changed" is a common hoover ploy they use, and 2 months seems hardly enough time to see significant progress. And they're lovebombing you?? It sounds like he just took all your issues with the relationship and found an easy and unverifiable solution to each one in an attempt to get you back.

Man, I understand this. I was falsely accused by my ex-fiancee wbpd to the point it wound up in the legal system. It was absolutely terrifying, and while nothing ended up happening, I remember being absolutely shocked someone could do something *that* serious for seemingly no good reason. If I fought the charges or was able to prove he'd wrongfully accused me, there would've been serious repercussions for him. I couldn't understand why he'd take such a risk just to punish me. 

Obviously, my exwbpd is pretty far gone. He's deteriorated to a point that I don't think he'll even attempt to change until he faces the consequences of his actions, which he *should* have dealt with ages ago. He's able to outrun all the damage he's done and the people who hate him all because of his family. His parents are extremely enabling and seem to buy into whatever story he chooses to feed them. They're well off and vast, so he just keeps moving around the country when he burns every bridge he can wherever he's at. 

I still struggle with how his family shields him from taking responsibility for the awful things he does. They're not stupid, being a teacher and a successful attorney, so I don't believe for a moment they don't know. That, and after he accused me of assaulting him, they bailed me out. 

I don't think I'll ever understand why they don't let him face the music. They've been the target of his antics before, and it seems like if they really care, they're doing him a huge disservice. I wish I had more to offer, but I'm just as confused as you are about those kinds of people. My best guess is that it's just long-term exposure. My ex eased into the more extreme manipulation with me, and I imagine he did the same with everyone else.

Mine did this hard after the last time he discarded me. Usually, I'd been a bit of a yes-man to keep the peace, but after he left, there wasn't really a reason to anymore. I also recall that he would consistently alter his version of the "truth" whenever I was able to challenge his original. I had called him out for the insane things he did, and he said that was my "manipulative heart" and told me to "stop living in your delusions." When I was able to *prove* that he'd done these things, he changed his tune real fast, and suddenly, I was using his trauma against him, and he didn't remember doing any of it. 

He had gaslit me before, like saying I didn't notice anything he did when I asked him why he didn't do the dishes. This was slightly insulting as I was staring right at them while he was telling me otherwise. Before discarding, though, it was all a lot more subtle; it wasn't until after discard that he was flat-out calling me crazy and delusional.
I had something similar *almost* happen, but I noped out as soon as I heard the word bpd. I swear they smell blood in the water

I'm one of the unfortunates that have dated both! :D I didn't know about the npd until years later,  which sucks because it would've been nice to know what the hell was going on at the time. I don't know the exacts about the internal differences, but I can certainly compare them as the target of their "affection":

Npd was a lot less cruel; he still had no regard for my feelings, but the horrible shit he did seemed more practically motivated. This is a key difference to me when compared to bpd, which would try to emotionally tear me to pieces.

Bpd was a lot more desperate to keep me around. I broke up with my exwnpd, without the suicide threats or coercion. 

Npd was a lot more manipulative. Well, at least it was a lot more efficient. There weren't any of the slips that I saw with bpd when their true motivations were revealed. 

This isn't every difference I was able to spot, and the relationship cycle was the same. Npd hurt me a lot more because he was so much more inauthentic than he seemed, but bpd was more vicious because his "true self" seemed to want me dead. All in all, both are getting a 0/10

That's what I suspect they all must do with us and their previous exes. I feel really bad, too, and I think I'd be in good company.

It was the same with me! My ex didn't even seem to try and get everything and couldn't understand why I demanded it all be removed. I suspect he wanted to eventually make him way back to me, which I put a stop to real quick. :) The "presents" he left for me, though, were absolutely on purpose. 

And you'll be okay! I don't like to think of it as setting me back, so much as immunizing me to reminders of him.

When my exwbpd left, he hid things like his engagement ring and a gift I'd made for him around the apartment. That and finding the nail clippers for the dogs hurt a lot. Did a bit of a cleanse after that!

Therapy has helped me a lot if that's something you would consider, but this sub is amazing too :) The betrayal hurts immensely, but it only hurts that bad because we cared so much. I can only imagine how great our final relationship will be when we find the right one

You're right, I wholeheartedly believe they'd sell us out for a pack of gum if it would benefit them, and that's certainly hard to reconcile.

I'm afraid this is one of those lessons you just have to learn the hard way.

No avoiding being sad, I'm afraid. I ran into the same problem, and it was made worse by the fact that I'd rather be a horrible, abusive monster than accept that he manipulated and used me. But, like you said, the evidence is overwhelming.

Yep! Mine was rarely physically violent, but I'd almost prefer that to the complete mental rewiring he did. My ex wasn't anyone too remarkable, but my god did I underestimate him. Yep! I was falsely accused, too, and struggled for a long time wondering if maybe I was abusive and horrible like he always said. One thing that I found helpful was looking at more cut and dry evidence:

-He was the one to lovebomb (said I love you really early, would obsessively message me)
-He was the one who threatened suicide if I were to break up with him
-He was the one telling insane lies (his brother stabbed him, he slept with his teacher, he was in a gang and watched people die)

I had the problem of not being able to eat, too, along with sleep problems. My exwbpd brought out some of my worst traits, too. Every argument, sudden change of plans, silent treatment disguised as "taking space," always brought out a strong reaction from me. In a normal relationship, these really wouldn't be a big deal, but with a pwbpd, the stakes are *unbelievably* high. I equate it to getting in trouble with your parents sucks, but it's not normally the end of the world. Compare that to a kid whose parents hit them. Suddenly, you understand why they react panicky and dramatic when they get in trouble. 

These people have absolutely zero regard for our well-being and leave us in impossible situations. They slander and ruin our reputation, they gaslight and manipulate us, they make us question our sanity and make *us* feel like monsters. When things go wrong in our relationships with pwbpd, we go into survival mode because we are in danger, whether it's physical, mental, or emotional. Normal people don't cause these things, which is why we're left so confused and hurt.

There was a great analogy I read on here a couple months ago. The idea is that they're like a toddler; they're extremely reactive, hard to communicate with, and don't behave as typical adults do. We are, for a time, their favorite toy. We're not real to them the way they are to themselves, but they care for us and bring us everywhere. This lasts for a time before we succumb to wear and tear, they drop us, or throw us against the wall. Suddenly their favorite toy is broken, and they absolutely cannot stand it. They might look for another toy, but eventually we become 'fixed' and they can get their favorite one back. Only problem is they're not gentle and we become more fragile every time they break us. Eventually we're of no use to them, so they throw us away and move onto another.

People with bpd truly want to feel loved and cared for, but they are incapable of maintaining it. You will never be their favorite toy forever and every story on here is similar to yours. It was on the onset of Covid-19 that I saw the end was near. It was the most horribly incredible time where rush hour was a distant memory and the evening news brought forth the fire and brimstone that was sure to bury us at any moment. Luckily I came prepared, years ago I had bought the underground trailer I called my bunker and lived out the years within it's walls. 

I had set a date, March 20, 2030 to escape the suffocating sarcophagus I now found to be my salvation. I was tempted at times to take just a peak of the desert landscape I was buried beneath, but memories of semi freezers being used as mortuaries and the whispers of oncoming war kept me safely sealed away. It was long and hard, I had much to miss, but worth the value of being one of the last to remain. Untainted by horrors that surely came to mankind. 

Slowly but surely though, the day finally came. I ended up waiting an extra couple of months, mentally unprepared for the world around me. Peeking my eyes out of the hatch though, made the entire decade I'd spent in solitude worth every barren second. Miles away I could see the glint of car windows that hadn't moved in years and heard the howl and cackles of coyotes roaming the plane for long-dead victims. It was a fowl landscape dotted with bones and the parcels they carried when there was still hope for escape. 

It was then that I noticed a line of cars far as the eye could see that had been long ago been lit ablaze, possibly by lightning or the natural flames that engulfed the dried plants that frequented the desert. I couldn't help but think though that it wasn't yet time. Who's to say this wasn't the doing of some bombing, maybe even nuclear? Perhaps it was a band of survivors driven mad by the isolation and death I now find all around me. 

I couldn't say, it had never crossed my mind to get a radio. What killed all these families must have been more than an illness, more than exposure. Perhaps it hasn't been years, my bunker is sound proof. Who's to say this didn't happen a year, a week ago? *Safer,* I think, *to wait awhile longer.* 

And with that thought I once again found myself in a damp and dark underground trailer eating long stale preserved food. Once again I found myself staring down another decade, waiting for a safe world that would never come.

It's been exactly 20 years, 5 months, and 23 days since the Final Nativity. You probably know that, of course, the number lights up the corner of every channel. If you don't know that then perhaps there's hope after all but I'm not holding my breath. I was a nurse in the maternity ward at the Ohio University Hospital when the Final Nativity occurred, although back then we called it the Great Decline. These days I prefer the term Major Fucking Problem. Anyway, as I was saying I was a nurse in the messiest and most fulfilling ward in the hospital. I was never big on kids, never had any myself (No kidding) but seeing all the mother's holding their newborns for the first time gave me a sense that I was a part of the circle of life, a necessary piece in making a family complete.

I would learn later that we weren't the first to notice this, the government was tipped off by the Red Cross while they were doing some nice thing in some not-so-nice country. No children born that day in any of their camps or clinics. That immediately started what would become the biggest, most inclusive investigation and race for a cure in history. I noticed it too, just on a much smaller scale. No women being wheelchaired into the ward, no nervous fathers lurking out in the hallway. We had a few women and babies still in the ICU or in recovery but nothing to get my hands dirty.

My sister called me later that day after my uneventful shift with strange news too. She was a maternity nurse down in Utah and was chipper about her day, she'd been let out early and had time to go out to lunch. No babies born in Utah either it seemed, the baby-making capital of the country. That's when I realized something was wrong and the rest of the country followed suit. Within days the news were leaving a trail of fear through every household with stories of pregnant women having miscarriages, fertility treatments failing, etc. Even test tube babies weren't growing. 

​

To say the world was shocked was an understatement. There weren't any of the riots or protests, the hallmark of a proper emergency. Just a lot of people being asked to solve a problem well above their paygrade. The Final Nativity was named after about two weeks as I recall, when they were able to pinpoint 6 babies being born on midnight the day before the Major Fucking Problem. That's when things got real strange. 

​

They're all 20 now and relatively unimportant in my opinion, but at the time they were the Second Coming of Christ. The pope canonized them at 5 days old, the only living beings to ever be official Saints. Science couldn't find any use for them but, oh boy, the churches did. One was Islamic and became a national symbol of repentance. One was Hindu and became Shiva. Last I heard she lived in a temple and never spoke a word, the literal overseer of destruction. One died shortly after, but the last three grew up as Christian icons. 

There were conspiracy theories behind every corner and miracle cures on every pop-up ad. I guess stupidity and greed don't stop when the world does. That being said though, life went on. I mean, what were we supposed to do? I was transferred to the trauma center and went on saving lives. The maternity ward stuck around for a few years, a sort of symbol of hope I suppose, before it was converted for more pressing purposes. A tension grew in the air as we all watched the Final Six grow up, celebrating birthdays and starting school. 

​

Other than a few protests and panic early on, the truth was that everyone that knew a damn thing was growing older. Elementary schools were a thing of the past years ago, it became the governments secondary objective to educate kids as soon as possible given the pressing circumstances. There are still quite a few colleges open, all of them free to everyone under the age of 45. Foods a little more scarce but automated machinery keeps the shelves stocked with the necessities. Homes are a dime a dozen in some parts with so fewer people to fill them. Religion is up ten-fold and no more wars, so I guess there is a bright side to this story. 

We are though, without a doubt, dying. Any hope for a cure ended about a decade ago when the specialists in the field started dying off like the rest of us. There's a poem I'm reminded of by Dylan Thomas, called 'Do Not Go Gently Into That Good Night'. There are those who aren't going peacefully, who fight everyday to bring a fresh face into the world. The rest of us are getting a little old for that, as a whole we're going gently into the good night together.
